sourceCheck: Pinned Angular v22, documentation build v22.2.1. The release page lists v22 as the current major; no v23 release is listed. Support table: v22 Active, released 2026-06-03, Active until 2027-06 and LTS until 2028-06; v21 LTS, released 2025-11-19, LTS until 2027-06; v20 LTS, released 2025-05-28, LTS until 2026-11-28. Versions v2–v19 are unsupported. Starting with v22, the cadence is one major every 12 months and 4–6 minors per major; previously it was one major every six months and 1–3 minors. Typical support is 24 months: 12 Active plus 12 LTS. Deprecated APIs remain available for at least one major, approximately one year. The listed v22.1–v23.0 schedule matches the supplied schedule. The compatibility page lists TypeScript >=6.0.0 <6.1.0 for Angular 22.0.x; no compatibility-range cards are planned. API status labels confirm Signal Forms form, FormField, submit and required, resource, rxResource, httpResource and injectAsync are stable since v22.0. Service is a decorator with no preview, experimental or deprecated notice, so it is stable under the specified rule. ChangeDetectionStrategy.Default remains a deprecated alias equivalent to Eager. The v22 and v20 blog posts opened successfully; the v21 post failed with Internal Error, including a retry. Both GitHub changelog pages opened; their file contents were checked through their raw representations. Angular entries 22.0.0, 22.1.0, 22.2.0, 21.2.0, 21.1.0 and 21.0.0, and CLI 22.0.0, confirm the relevant defaults, stabilizations, deprecations and removals. Consecutive cases and template spread landed in 21.1; expression-bodied arrows and exhaustive switch checks in 21.2; optional-chaining undefined behavior and nested-union exhaustive checks in 22.0. Opened API pages under https://angular.dev, with braces denoting individually opened paths: /api/core/{Component,ViewEncapsulation,HostBinding,HostListener,Pipe,NgModule,ViewChild,@let,@if,@for,@switch,@defer,signal,WritableSignal,computed,untracked,linkedSignal,effect,EffectRef,CreateEffectOptions,resource,Resource,ResourceStatus,ResourceLoaderParams,ResourceStreamingLoader,input,InputSignal,model,output,OutputEmitterRef,viewChild,viewChildren,contentChild,contentChildren,booleanAttribute,numberAttribute,inject,Injectable,Service,InjectionToken,injectAsync,runInInjectionContext,InjectOptions,EnvironmentInjector,ChangeDetectionStrategy,provideZoneChangeDetection,provideZonelessChangeDetection,NgZone,ChangeDetectorRef,PendingTasks,DestroyRef,afterNextRender,afterEveryRender,afterRenderEffect,SimpleChanges,OnChanges,OnInit,DoCheck,AfterContentInit,AfterViewInit,REQUEST,RESPONSE_INIT}; /api/core/rxjs-interop/{toSignal,toObservable,rxResource}; /api/core/testing/{TestBed,DeferBlockBehavior,DeferBlockFixture}; /api/common/{NgIf,NgClass,NgStyle,AsyncPipe}; /api/common/http/{httpResource,HttpClient,provideHttpClient,withXhr,HttpParams,HttpHeaders,HttpRequest,HttpContext,HttpContextToken,withRequestsMadeViaParent,withXsrfConfiguration,withNoXsrfProtection,HttpInterceptorFn,withInterceptors,withInterceptorsFromDi}; /api/router/{provideRouter,Route,ActivatedRoute,withComponentInputBinding,ExtraOptions,CanActivateFn,CanMatchFn,ResolveFn,RouterLinkActive}; /api/forms/{FormControl,FormGroup,FormRecord,NonNullableFormBuilder,NgModel}; /api/forms/signals/{form,FormField,submit,required}; /api/platform-browser/{provideClientHydration,withNoIncrementalHydration}. Qualifications for the section descriptions: rxResource uses a stream option rather than a loader option. The effect API describes root effects as microtasks, so the plan avoids a blanket change-detection timing claim. ResourceStatus's error row conflicts with the resource guide's explicit throwing behavior; the error-guard fact follows the guide. Signal Forms restricts structural containers to plain objects and arrays, while custom-control leaf values may use other types. submit ignores pending validators by default, so the plan tests failed validation rather than claiming that pending validation blocks submission. The Pipe API retains a legacy NgModule-only descriptive sentence; standalone usage follows the current component and pipe guides. No section otherwise requires removal.

cards.statement: Angular resolves a relative styleUrl from the workspace root.
cards.explanation: Angular resolves styleUrl relative to the directory containing the component file.

cards.statement: A component's imports array exposes its imported pipes to its template.
cards.explanation: List a pipe in the component's imports so Angular recognizes it in that component's template.

cards.statement: Since Angular v19, @Component defaults to standalone: false.
cards.explanation: Components are standalone by default. A component declared in an NgModule uses standalone: false.

cards.statement: Angular creates a separate component instance for each matching template element.
cards.explanation: Repeated uses of a component selector produce distinct instances with their own component state.

cards.statement: Angular replaces a component's host element with the component's rendered view.
cards.explanation: Angular keeps the host element and renders the component's template inside it.

cards.statement: Angular's documentation recommends host metadata over @HostBinding and @HostListener.
cards.explanation: The host property centralizes host bindings; the decorators remain for backwards compatibility.

cards.statement: Angular uses ng-content's select attribute to route matching children to a projection slot.
cards.explanation: The select attribute filters projected content using Angular's supported selector syntax.

cards.statement: Angular appends ng-content fallback content after the matching projected children.
cards.explanation: Angular displays a slot's fallback content when that slot receives no matching child content.

cards.statement: Placing ng-content inside @if postpones projected content creation until the condition becomes truthy.
cards.explanation: Angular creates projected content even when its ng-content placeholder is hidden. The guide advises against conditional ng-content.

cards.statement: Angular uses ViewEncapsulation.Emulated when a component leaves encapsulation unspecified.
cards.explanation: Angular scopes component styles by adding generated attributes to template elements and style selectors.

cards.statement: ViewEncapsulation.Emulated isolates component elements from matching global style rules.
cards.explanation: Global styles can still affect elements inside a component using Emulated encapsulation.

cards.statement: Angular's style guide prefers protected for template-only component members.
cards.explanation: Using protected keeps template helpers out of the component class's public API.

cards.statement: Angular converts an interpolated expression's value to a string for rendering.
cards.explanation: Text interpolation renders the string representation of the evaluated value.

source.title: Binding dynamic text, properties and attributes

cards.statement: Angular writes an empty string to an attr. binding's attribute when its value is null.
cards.explanation: A null attribute-binding value makes Angular remove the attribute.

source.title: Binding dynamic text, properties and attributes

cards.statement: Angular's style guide prefers NgClass over class bindings for template styling.
cards.explanation: The style guide prefers built-in class bindings over NgClass.

cards.statement: Angular exposes the triggering event as $event inside a template event listener.
cards.explanation: A listener passes $event to a handler when that handler needs the event's details.

cards.statement: Angular writes two-way binding with parentheses inside square brackets, as in [(value)].
cards.explanation: The [(...)] form combines the property's binding with the corresponding event binding.

cards.statement: Angular assigns an unqualified #ref on a component element to that element's native DOM node.
cards.explanation: On an Angular component, an unqualified template reference holds the component instance.

cards.statement: Angular keeps an @let variable current as the declaration's template expression changes.
cards.explanation: An @let declaration follows its expression like a binding instead of preserving an initial snapshot.

cards.statement: A pure pipe reruns when Angular checks an array input that was mutated in place.
cards.explanation: A pure pipe detects a changed input value or reference, rather than mutations within the same array.

cards.statement: In `ready ? a : b | format`, Angular pipes the entire conditional result through format.
cards.explanation: Angular reads `ready ? a : b | format` as `ready ? a : (b | format)` because a pipe binds more tightly than a ternary.
cards.misconception: Ternaries bind more tightly than pipes.

cards.statement: Angular template expressions support parseInt as a built-in global function.
cards.explanation: The supported globals are undefined and $any. Expose other functions through the component when needed.

cards.statement: Angular template expressions support arrow functions that use an expression body.
cards.explanation: Template arrow functions use an expression after =>; block-bodied arrow functions are rejected.

cards.statement: Since Angular v22, template optional chaining yields undefined for a nullish receiver.
cards.explanation: Angular's template ?. operator returns undefined when its receiver is null or undefined.

cards.statement: An @if as alias holds the condition's evaluated result inside the rendered block.
cards.explanation: The alias exposes the expression result, such as a user object, for reuse within that branch.

cards.statement: An @for block supports a Set of items as the collection it renders in a template.
cards.explanation: @for accepts JavaScript iterables, including Set, while Angular optimizes Array iteration.

cards.statement: Angular requires a track expression when compiling an @for block.
cards.explanation: A missing track expression is a compilation error because Angular needs a key for associating items with views.

cards.statement: Angular's documentation recommends track $index for lists that reorder their items.
cards.explanation: The guide recommends a unique item property for changing collections; $index suits static collections.

cards.statement: An @for view is recreated when its tracked key changes on the same object.
cards.explanation: When the object reference stays the same, @for updates the view's bindings instead of recreating the view.

cards.statement: An @for track expression accepts the loop's contextual $count value.
cards.explanation: Track expressions use the item, $index or its alias, and component members. $count is outside that permitted context.

cards.statement: Angular renders an @for block's @empty content when its collection has no items.
cards.explanation: The @empty block supplies the empty-list view for that @for collection.

cards.statement: An @for block supports break for ending template iteration early.
cards.explanation: Angular's @for block rejects break statements; express the desired collection in the data supplied to the block.

cards.statement: Angular uses == to compare an @switch value with its case expressions.
cards.explanation: @switch compares each case expression with the switch value using ===.

cards.statement: Consecutive @case blocks can select a shared content block inside an @switch.
cards.explanation: List consecutive cases before one body to render that body for any of those matching values.

cards.statement: Exhaustive @switch checks support a signal call as the switch expression.
cards.explanation: Exhaustiveness checks rely on narrowing a variable. A direct signal read as the switch expression does not support that check.

cards.statement: In Angular v20 and later, NgIf is deprecated in favor of the @if block.
cards.explanation: NgIf remains present in Angular v22 with a deprecation notice directing users to @if.
cards.volatilityNote: NgIf remains in v22, but its API declares intent to remove it in a future major release.

cards.statement: Angular lazily loads an NgModule-declared component used directly inside @defer.
cards.explanation: Direct NgModule-based dependencies of @defer load eagerly.

cards.statement: Referencing a deferred component's class in a same-file ViewChild query makes its code load eagerly.
cards.explanation: Same-file ViewChild class references defeat that dependency's @defer splitting.

cards.statement: Angular eagerly loads the dependencies used in an @defer block's @loading content.
cards.explanation: @loading content belongs to the eager bundle.

cards.statement: The after option of @loading postpones Angular's deferred dependency fetch.
cards.explanation: @loading's after postpones its display, rather than fetching.

cards.statement: Angular starts a @placeholder minimum timer when that placeholder first renders.
cards.explanation: A placeholder's minimum display interval begins with its initial render.

cards.statement: Angular uses on viewport as the default trigger for an unconfigured @defer block.
cards.explanation: An unconfigured @defer starts loading when the browser becomes idle.

cards.statement: For on viewport, Angular watches the @placeholder element by default.
cards.explanation: @defer uses its placeholder as the implicit viewport target.

cards.statement: Angular can use a multi-root @placeholder as the implicit on interaction target.
cards.explanation: An implicit interaction target requires one placeholder root element.

cards.statement: A @defer when condition restores the placeholder after changing back to false.
cards.explanation: @defer's when activates once; subsequent falsy values leave content displayed.

cards.statement: Angular prefetches @defer dependencies separately from the trigger that renders the block.
cards.explanation: Prefetch loads the code; the regular on or when trigger controls rendering.

cards.statement: With HMR active, Angular waits for @defer triggers before fetching their chunks.
cards.explanation: HMR fetches @defer chunks eagerly, bypassing configured triggers.
cards.volatilityNote: HMR's eager chunk-fetching behavior is tooling behavior that may change in later releases.

cards.statement: A barrel import can keep a deferred component in the application's main bundle.
cards.explanation: Barrel exports may defeat @defer chunk splitting.
cards.volatilityNote: Lazy chunk splitting through barrels depends on compiler and bundler behavior that may change.
